findings.summary: Regression from 1.0.0, caused by the update's new long-form rule. In-article figures that stand for a diagram or a screenshot are now replaced by one large pictogram of a loosely related object, and the drawing no longer shows what its caption says. A caption about an inventory board of grouped components sits under a single sewing button. A caption about one release written for two audiences sits under a pencil. Both are full text-column plates holding a 416px drawing in the middle of the prose. In 1.0.0 the same figures were ghosted UI previews on a stage: a grid of grouped tiles, and two side-by-side panels. Those matched their captions and followed the reference's habit of putting UI on stages. The cause is the new line in Layout adaptation: 'An image without a photo becomes a drawing of the page's or item's own subject (Imagery), never removed.' It treats every missing image as an item photo. The rc.3 distinction ('diagrams and screenshots sit on a stage') is gone.
findings.promptFix: Split the missing-image rule by what the image is for. (1) An image that stands for a thing (an item, a person's object, the subject of a page) becomes that thing's own drawing, on a plate or drawing stage. (2) An image that stands for information (a diagram, a screenshot, a comparison, a chart; usually it has a caption that describes structure or data) becomes a ghosted UI preview or a simple diagram on a stage, built from the system's own surfaces (raised cards, hairlines, skeleton bars), never a pictogram. In Verification, add: 'Read each figure's caption: the figure must show what the caption describes; a caption about a layout, list, board or comparison never sits under a single object drawing.'

findings.summary: Regression from 1.0.0, caused by the update's rewrite of the stat-row rule. At 390px the four stat cards (a label, one number, a delta) now stack one per row as full-width cards. Together they take about 540 CSS px, more than half a phone screen, before the first chart. 1.0.0 showed them 2x2, a fix added after an earlier critic round ('Stat cards: 2 per row under breakpoint.md'). The new wording, 'Stat rows wrap evenly whatever their count (equal columns, never one card alone on the last row)', is satisfied by one column, so the density rule is lost.
findings.promptFix: Restore the density floor in general terms. 'Short metric cards (a label, a value, an optional change) sit at least two per row at every width, so four make 2x2 under breakpoint.md. Rows wrap evenly, never with one card alone on the last row. Only cards that hold a chart, a list or a form take a full row on a phone.' Add to Verification: 'At 390px, no full-width card holds only one number.'

findings.summary: One plate fails the one-word test. The tea-towel product is drawn as a lidded canister with a hanging loop, with no fold, fringe or stripe that says cloth. It reads as a bin or jar. The reference's small objects read at once (hanger, toolbox).

In the pending state, the working glyph sits beside the 'Refreshing…' label instead of replacing it. The spec says the glyph sits inside the button and replaces the label, never beside it. The agent kept the wording on purpose.
On wide screens the posts search field is placed visually to the right of the filter chips but comes first in the tab order, so keyboard focus runs against the visual order. The agent reported this.
On the item detail screen there is about 90px of empty paper between the header lede and the tab bar, a larger gap than any other header-to-content gap in the family. It reads as a missing block.

notes: Update goal (overfit review: written for any product, not for the four demo apps). Mostly reached. The generalized wording still produces every placement the published version had: a header drawing plus a write-in h1 on every product screen, item detail included; the dashboard's primary chart on one stage; offer cards on a stage that stack fully at 390px; the featured post on a drawing stage beside its text; plates holding each item's own drawing, with a stable color per item; a transaction summary in a sticky side column. Two rewrites lost behavior that 1.0.0 had. They are the two majors: figures standing for information became object drawings, and short stat cards lost their two-per-row floor on phones. The verdict is therefore not a pass: both majors are spec-caused and there is one sample.

Earlier verdict (1.0.0 critic-4: no blockers; its weaknesses were signature-level). Fixed or not seen again in this sample: the about page's prose opener is now centred over the h1 (blog about-desktop-light). The numeric BUDGET header now ends on its cells' right edge (dashboard home-desktop-light). No bell is reused for a team screen; Team draws a handheld radio (team-desktop-dark). The key-ring plate no longer reads as a creature (commerce home-d10). The swatch-fan-as-shell is gone; the featured post is a hand pressing a stamp (blog home-d2). Side grips now wrap the handle as loops (blog home-d2 stamp, commerce home-d1 tote), closer to reference p10-i5. Carried minors are not re-raised: dark off-switch thumb (settings-notifications-desktop-dark) and invoice column spread (settings-billing-desktop-light).

Measured layout defects: none listed. Harness capture artifacts, not counted: the sticky header painted mid-page in full-page state captures (blog state-search-empty, state-newsletter-error; dashboard state-empty-filter; settings state-profile-errors-mobile-light); the dialog scrim ending at 900px (settings state-plan-dialog-desktop-light). The block-rise gaps that the blog, dashboard and settings agents warned about do not appear: every below-the-fold block is visible in the full-page shots (settings-billing-desktop-light shows Payment method and Invoices).

Gates: all passed on all four apps. Smoke tests were not run for this screen (they run at the confirm step); each agent reports its own suite passing. Palette consistency 0.823, type consistency 0.811.

Reference fidelity 4. Cream paper and warm ink, a serif display over a quiet sans, ink and stone ring controls, pastel stages crossed by faint wandering lines, and cel drawings that step in stroke by stroke and hold. Compare blog motion-m2 and dashboard motion-m1 with the reference's stepped drawings, and blog home-desktop-light with reference p1/p3 section openers. Nothing is copied: no reference subjects, names or marks.

Signature 3.5. All five elements are in all four apps, and motion steps once and holds (frames = strokes + boil; commerce products-canvas-field-tote-m2, settings-billing-m2). The working glyph is now visible in a real pending state (dashboard state-loading). Craft is close to 1.0.0's or better: large strokes taper, and hands come from several edges in different poses (commerce home-d1, blog home-d3/d7, settings billing-d2/d4). It is held down by the figure regression (major) and one weak plate (minor).

Hierarchy 4: every screen leads with the serif h1 and its drawing, then one stage or main card. The 416px drawings inside articles compete with the lead image; that is counted in the figure major, not here. Cross-app 4: one family across the four apps in light and dark (commerce home-desktop-dark, dashboard team-desktop-dark, settings settings-notifications-desktop-dark). Component states 4: clay focus rings, danger rings with inline messages and an 'N fields need attention' line, a designed dialog, empty states with a drawing and one action, skeleton loading with the glyph. Polish 4: no browser-default leftovers.
